results.title: Binary decision diagram
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: A binary decision diagram, in tree form, is either a leaf carrying a Boolean value, or a node consisting of a variable $v \in \mathbb{N}$ and two diagrams: the low child, for $v$ false, and the high child, for $v$ true.

results.title: Evaluation of a binary decision diagram
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Under an assignment $\sigma$ of a Boolean value to each variable $v \in \mathbb{N}$, the value of a leaf is its Boolean value, and the value of a node testing $v$ is the value of its high child if $\sigma(v)$ is true and the value of its low child if $\sigma(v)$ is false.

results.title: Size of a diagram
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The size of a diagram is its number of leaves and nodes, counted in tree form: a leaf has size $1$, and a node with children $\ell$ and $h$ has size one more than the sum of the sizes of $\ell$ and $h$.

results.title: Diagrams ordered from a variable
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, a diagram is ordered from $n$ when every variable it tests is at least $n$ and the tested variables strictly increase along every path. Recursively: every leaf is ordered from $n$, and the node testing $v$ with children $\ell$ and $h$ is ordered from $n$ when $n \le v$ and both $\ell$ and $h$ are ordered from $v + 1$.

results.title: Reduced diagrams
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A diagram is reduced when no node in it has two equal children: every leaf is reduced, and the node testing $v$ with children $\ell$ and $h$ is reduced when $\ell \ne h$ and both $\ell$ and $h$ are reduced.

results.title: Reduced ordered binary decision diagram
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A binary decision diagram is a reduced ordered binary decision diagram (ROBDD), for the natural order on variables, when it is ordered from $0$ (the tested variables strictly increase along every path) and reduced (no node has two equal children).

results.title: Independence from variables below the order
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a binary decision diagram ordered from $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $v < n$ be a variable. For every assignment $\sigma$ of Boolean values to the variables and every Boolean $b$, the value of $t$ under $\sigma[v \mapsto b]$ (the assignment $\sigma$ with $v$ set to $b$) equals the value of $t$ under $\sigma$.

results.title: Fixing the top variable of an ordered node
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a node testing the variable $v$ with low child $\ell$ and high child $h$, and suppose $t$ is ordered from some $n \in \mathbb{N}$. For every assignment $\sigma$ of Boolean values to the variables and every Boolean $b$, the value of $t$ under $\sigma[v \mapsto b]$ (the assignment $\sigma$ with $v$ set to $b$) is the value of $h$ under $\sigma$ if $b$ is true, and the value of $\ell$ under $\sigma$ if $b$…

results.title: Binary decision diagrams have positive size
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every binary decision diagram $t$, the size of $t$ (its number of leaves and nodes, counted in tree form) is strictly positive.

results.title: Canonicity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Canonicity (Bryant): two reduced ordered diagrams with the same function are equal.

results.title: Reduced ordered diagrams are equal iff they have the same values
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $t_1$ and $t_2$ are reduced ordered binary decision diagrams, then $t_1 = t_2$ if and only if $t_1$ and $t_2$ have the same value under every assignment of Boolean values to the variables.

results.title: Unsatisfiable reduced ordered diagrams
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A reduced ordered binary decision diagram $t$ is the leaf with value false if and only if $t$ has value false under every assignment of Boolean values to the variables.

results.title: Node constructor removing a redundant test
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a variable $v \in \mathbb{N}$ and diagrams $\ell$ and $h$, the diagram $\mathrm{mk}(v, \ell, h)$ is $\ell$ if $\ell = h$, and otherwise the node that tests $v$ with $\ell$ as its false-child and $h$ as its true-child.

results.title: Bryant's apply operation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a binary Boolean operation $\mathrm{op}$ and binary decision diagrams $t_1, t_2$, the diagram $A_{\mathrm{op}}(t_1, t_2)$ is defined by recursion. If $t_1$ and $t_2$ are leaves with values $a$ and $b$, it is the leaf with value $\mathrm{op}(a, b)$. Otherwise let $v$ be the smallest variable tested at the root of $t_1$ or of $t_2$ (a leaf tests none), and for $i = 1, 2$ let $\ell_i$ and $h_i$ be the low and high…

results.title: Apply computes the operation pointwise
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every binary Boolean operation $\mathrm{op}$, all binary decision diagrams $t_1$ and $t_2$, and every assignment $\sigma$ of Boolean values to the variables, the value under $\sigma$ of the diagram $\mathrm{apply}(\mathrm{op}, t_1, t_2)$ obtained from $t_1$ and $t_2$ by Bryant's apply operation under $\mathrm{op}$ is $\mathrm{op}(a_1, a_2)$, where $a_i$ is the value of $t_i$ under $\sigma$.

results.title: Apply preserves orderedness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathrm{op}$ be a binary Boolean operation and $n$ a natural number. If the diagrams $t_1$ and $t_2$ are both ordered from $n$, then the result of apply with $\mathrm{op}$ on $t_1$ and $t_2$ is ordered from $n$.

results.title: Apply returns reduced diagrams
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every binary Boolean operation $\mathrm{op}$ and all diagrams $t_1$ and $t_2$, the result of apply with $\mathrm{op}$ on $t_1$ and $t_2$ is reduced.

results.title: Diagram of a proposition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Each proposition $A$ whose atoms are natural numbers is sent to a binary decision diagram by recursion on $A$: an atom $x$ goes to the node testing $x$ with the leaf false as its false-child and the leaf true as its true-child, and a conjunction $A \wedge B$, disjunction $A \vee B$ or implication $A \to B$ goes to the result of apply on the diagrams of $A$ and $B$ under the Boolean operation and, or, or…

results.title: Equal BDDs iff equal truth tables
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For propositions $A$ and $B$ over natural-number atoms, the binary decision diagrams of $A$ and $B$ are equal if and only if $A$ and $B$ have the same truth value under every valuation $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$.

results.title: Satisfiable iff the BDD is not the false leaf
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a proposition $A$ over natural-number atoms, the binary decision diagram of $A$ is not the leaf false if and only if some valuation $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ makes $A$ true.

path: Scott-continuous maps and least fixed points

results.title: Scott continuity into a function space is checked pointwise
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ be ω-complete partial orders, and let $g$ be a map from $\alpha$ to the ω-complete partial order of Scott-continuous maps $\beta \to \gamma$, ordered pointwise. If for every $b \in \beta$ the map $a \mapsto g(a)(b)$ is Scott-continuous, then $g$ is Scott-continuous. Here a map is Scott-continuous when it is monotone and preserves suprema of ω-chains.

results.title: Currying of Scott-continuous maps
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ be ω-complete partial orders and let $f : \alpha \times \beta \to \gamma$ be a Scott-continuous map, that is, a map that is monotone and preserves suprema of ω-chains. Its currying is the Scott-continuous map from $\alpha$ to the ω-complete partial order of Scott-continuous maps $\beta \to \gamma$, ordered pointwise, that sends $a$ to the map $b \mapsto f(a, b)$.

results.title: Least fixed point of a Scott-continuous map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $D$ be an ω-complete partial order with a least element $\bot$, and let $f : D \to D$ be Scott-continuous, that is, monotone and preserving suprema of ω-chains. The least fixed point $\operatorname{lfp} f$ of $f$ is the supremum of the Kleene chain $\bot \le f(\bot) \le f(f(\bot)) \le \cdots$, whose $n$-th term is the $n$-fold iterate $f^n(\bot)$.

results.title: The least fixed point is a fixed point
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $D$ be an ω-complete partial order with a least element $\bot$, and let $f : D \to D$ be Scott-continuous, that is, monotone and preserving suprema of ω-chains. Then the least fixed point $\operatorname{lfp} f$ of $f$ satisfies $f(\operatorname{lfp} f) = \operatorname{lfp} f$.

results.title: The least fixed point lies below every prefixed point
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $D$ be an ω-complete partial order with a least element $\bot$, let $f : D \to D$ be Scott-continuous, that is, monotone and preserving suprema of ω-chains, and let $\operatorname{lfp} f$ be the supremum of the Kleene chain $\bot \le f(\bot) \le f(f(\bot)) \le \cdots$. If $a \in D$ satisfies $f(a) \le a$, then $\operatorname{lfp} f \le a$.

results.title: Scott continuity of the least-fixed-point operator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $D$ be an ω-complete partial order with a least element $\bot$. For a Scott-continuous map $f : D \to D$, that is, one that is monotone and preserves suprema of ω-chains, let $\operatorname{lfp} f$ be its least fixed point. The map $f \mapsto \operatorname{lfp} f$, from the ω-complete partial order of Scott-continuous maps $D \to D$, ordered pointwise, to $D$, is Scott-continuous.

results.title: The least-fixed-point operator as a Scott-continuous map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $D$ be an ω-complete partial order with a least element $\bot$. The least-fixed-point operator, sending a Scott-continuous map $f : D \to D$ to its least fixed point $\operatorname{lfp} f$, bundled as a Scott-continuous map from the ω-complete partial order of Scott-continuous maps $D \to D$, ordered pointwise, to $D$.

results.title: Binomial (Hurwitz) product of power series
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K$ be a commutative ring. The binomial product of formal power series $A = \sum_n a_n X^n$ and $B = \sum_n b_n X^n$ in $K[[X]]$ is the power series $\sum_n c_n X^n$ with $c_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k} a_k b_{n-k}$.

results.title: Coefficients of the binomial product
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a commutative ring and let $A = \sum_n a_n X^n$ and $B = \sum_n b_n X^n$ be formal power series over $K$. For every natural number $n$, the coefficient of $X^n$ in the binomial product of $A$ and $B$ is $\sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k} a_k b_{n-k}$.

results.title: Constant coefficient of the binomial product
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a commutative ring. For formal power series $A$ and $B$ over $K$, the constant coefficient of the binomial product of $A$ and $B$ is the product of the constant coefficients of $A$ and $B$.

results.title: Rationality of power series descends from field extensions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $G$ be a field extension of $F$ (a field with an $F$-algebra structure), and let $A$ be a power series over $F$. If there are polynomials $p$, $q$ over $G$ with $q \ne 0$ and $A q = p$, where $A$ is viewed as a power series over $G$, then there are polynomials $P$, $Q$ over $F$ with $Q \ne 0$ and $A Q = P$.

results.title: Orthogonal vectors descend from field extensions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $G$ be a field extension of $F$ (a field with an $F$-algebra structure), let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $S \subseteq F^n$. If some nonzero $t \in G^n$ satisfies $\sum_{i=1}^n s_i t_i = 0$ in $G$ for every $s \in S$, then some nonzero $u \in F^n$ satisfies $\sum_{i=1}^n s_i u_i = 0$ for every $s \in S$.

results.title: Negated-remainder sequence with fuel
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For real polynomials $a$, $b$ and a natural number $n$, this is the list of polynomials defined recursively by: for $n = 0$ it is the one-entry list $(a)$; for fuel $n + 1$ it is $(a)$ if $b = 0$, and otherwise it is $a$ followed by the list for the pair $b$, $-(a \bmod b)$ with fuel $n$, where $a \bmod b$ is the remainder of $a$ on division by $b$.

results.title: Sturm chain
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Sturm chain of a real polynomial $p$ is the list $p_0, p_1, \dots, p_m$ with $p_0 = p$, $p_1 = p'$ and $p_{k+1} = -(p_{k-1} \bmod p_k)$, the negated remainder of $p_{k-1}$ on division by $p_k$, where the list stops at $p_m$ as soon as the next entry would be $0$; thus $p_m$ is its last entry and, for $p \ne 0$, every entry is nonzero. For $p = 0$ the chain is the one-entry list $(0)$.

results.title: Number of sign changes in a list of reals
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $x_1, \dots, x_n$ of real numbers, let $y_1, \dots, y_m$ be the entries of the list that are nonzero, in their original order. The number of sign changes of the list is the number of indices $i$ with $1 \le i < m$ and $y_i y_{i+1} < 0$, that is, the number of adjacent pairs of opposite sign once the zeros are removed.

results.title: Sturm sign-variation function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real polynomial $p$ with Sturm chain $p_0, p_1, \dots, p_m$ and a real number $x$, $\sigma_p(x)$ is the number of sign changes, ignoring zeros, in the sequence of values $p_0(x), p_1(x), \dots, p_m(x)$.

results.title: Sturm's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a squarefree real polynomial and let $a < b$ be real numbers with $p(a) \ne 0$ and $p(b) \ne 0$. Then the number of distinct real roots $x$ of $p$ with $a < x < b$ equals $\sigma_p(a) - \sigma_p(b)$, where $\sigma_p$ is the Sturm sign-variation function of $p$ and the subtraction is truncated subtraction of natural numbers.

results.title: Left-orderable groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is left-orderable if it admits a linear order $\le$ such that $a \le b$ implies $ca \le cb$ for all $a, b, c \in G$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 15.49 (unique product groups and left orders)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement, asked by P. Linnell, that there exists a group $G$ with unique products that is not left-orderable. Here $G$ has unique products if for all finite nonempty subsets $X, Y \subseteq G$ there are $x_0 \in X$ and $y_0 \in Y$ such that $(x_0, y_0)$ is the only pair $(x, y) \in X \times Y$ with $xy = x_0 y_0$.

results.title: A unique product group need not be left-orderable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exists a group $G$ that has unique products but is not left-orderable: for all finite nonempty subsets $X, Y \subseteq G$ there are $x_0 \in X$ and $y_0 \in Y$ such that $(x_0, y_0)$ is the only pair $(x, y) \in X \times Y$ with $xy = x_0 y_0$, and yet $G$ admits no linear order invariant under left multiplication.

results.title: Number of residue classes met by an integer tuple
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an $m$-tuple $b = (b_1, \dots, b_m)$ of integers and a natural number $p$, $v_p(b)$ is the number of distinct values among the remainders $b_1 \bmod p, \dots, b_m \bmod p$, that is, the number of residue classes modulo $p$ that contain an entry of $b$.

results.title: Hardy–Littlewood admissible tuples
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An $m$-tuple $b$ of integers is admissible when $v_p(b) \ne p$ for every prime $p$, where $v_p(b)$ is the number of residue classes modulo $p$ that contain an entry of $b$.

results.title: The prime-tuple counting function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an $m$-tuple $b = (b_1, \dots, b_m)$ of integers and a natural number $x$, $P(x; b)$ is the number of integers $n$ with $1 \le n \le x$ such that each of $n + b_1, \dots, n + b_m$ is a (positive) prime number.

results.title: The Hardy–Littlewood singular series

results.title: Admissible finite sets of integers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite set $H$ of integers is admissible if for every prime $p$ there is a residue class $r$ modulo $p$ that contains no element of $H$.

results.title: Missing a residue class modulo a prime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $b = (b_1, \dots, b_m)$ be an $m$-tuple of integers, let $p$ be a prime, and let $v_p(b)$ be the number of residue classes modulo $p$ that contain an entry of $b$. Then $v_p(b) \ne p$ if and only if there is a residue class $r$ modulo $p$ with $b_i \not\equiv r \pmod p$ for every $i$.

results.title: Hardy–Littlewood admissibility via the set of entries
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A tuple of integers is Hardy–Littlewood admissible exactly when its set of entries is admissible.

results.title: The empty set is admissible
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The empty set of integers is admissible: for every prime $p$, some residue class modulo $p$ contains none of its elements.

results.title: The set $\{0\}$ is admissible
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The one-element set $\{0\}$ of integers is admissible: for every prime $p$ it misses the residue class of $1$ modulo $p$.

results.title: Ramanujan τ-function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, $\tau(n)$ is the complex number given by the coefficient of $q^n$ in the $q$-expansion of the modular discriminant $\Delta = \eta^{24}$, where $\eta$ is the Dedekind eta function and $q = e^{2\pi i z}$.

results.title: Normalisation of the Ramanujan τ-function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Ramanujan τ-function satisfies $\tau(1) = 1$: the coefficient of $q$ in the $q$-expansion of the modular discriminant $\Delta$ is $1$.

results.title: Ramanujan–Petersson conjecture for τ (Deligne's theorem)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every prime $p$, the Ramanujan τ-function satisfies $|\tau(p)| \le 2p^{11/2}$, where $|\cdot|$ is the absolute value of a complex number.

results.title: Number of representations by a vector of generators
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $a_1, \dots, a_k$ and an integer $m$, the representation count $d(m; a_1, \dots, a_k)$ is the number of tuples $(x_1, \dots, x_k)$ of natural numbers with $x_1 a_1 + \dots + x_k a_k = m$, counted as an extended natural number, so that it is $\infty$ when there are infinitely many such tuples.

results.title: Negative integers have no representations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $a_1, \dots, a_k$ and every integer $m < 0$, the representation count $d(m; a_1, \dots, a_k)$ is $0$.

results.title: Finitely many representations for positive generators
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $a_1, \dots, a_k$ are positive natural numbers, then for every integer $m$ the representation count $d(m; a_1, \dots, a_k)$ is finite.

results.title: Generalized Frobenius number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $a_1, \dots, a_k$ and $s$, write $d(m; a)$ for the number of representations of an integer $m$ by $a = (a_1, \dots, a_k)$. An integer $g$ is the generalized Frobenius number $g(a; s) = \max \{m \in \mathbb{Z} \mid d(m; a) \le s\}$ when $d(g; a) \le s$ and $d(m; a) > s$ for every integer $m > g$.

results.title: Uniqueness of the generalized Frobenius number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $a_1, \dots, a_k$ and $s$, if the integers $g$ and $g'$ are both the generalized Frobenius number $g(a_1, \dots, a_k; s)$, then $g = g'$.

results.title: Chain polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite partially ordered set $P$ and each natural number $k$, let $c_k(P)$ be the number of $k$-element chains of $P$, that is, of $k$-element subsets of $P$ any two of whose elements are comparable; in particular $c_0(P) = 1$, counting the empty chain. The chain polynomial of $P$ is the polynomial $C(P, t) = \sum_{k \ge 0} c_k(P)\, t^k$ with integer coefficients.

results.title: Stanley's Problem 20' has a negative answer

results.title: Parent vertex towards a root in a connected graph

results.title: Internally disjoint walks
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two walks $p$ and $q$ in a simple graph $G$ are internally disjoint if no vertex is an interior vertex of both, where the interior vertices of a walk are the entries of its vertex sequence other than the first and the last.

results.title: Infinitely connected graphs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A simple graph $G$ is infinitely connected if it has at least two vertices and, for any two distinct vertices $u$ and $v$, there is an infinite set of paths from $u$ to $v$ in $G$ that are pairwise internally disjoint.

results.title: One round of breadth-first search
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set and a set $s$ of vertices, this is the set of vertices that lie in $s$ or are adjacent to some vertex of $s$, that is, $s$ together with all neighbours of its vertices.

results.title: Breadth-first search with a round limit
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set, a natural number $n$ and a set $s$ of vertices, this applies rounds of breadth-first search to $s$ (each round adds all neighbours of the current vertices), stopping after $n$ rounds or as soon as a round adds no new vertex, whichever comes first, and returns the resulting set.

results.title: Vertices reachable from a vertex
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set $V$ and a vertex $u$, this is the set obtained from $\{u\}$ by breadth-first search with at most $|V|$ rounds, stopping early as soon as a round adds no new vertex.

results.title: Instances of single-machine scheduling with release times and deadlines
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A release-deadlines instance is a list of jobs $(p_0, r_0, d_0), \dots, (p_{n-1}, r_{n-1}, d_{n-1})$ of triples of natural numbers, where $p_j$ is the processing time, $r_j$ the release time and $d_j$ the deadline of job $j$.

results.title: Feasible single-machine schedules with release times and deadlines
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A release-deadlines instance with jobs $(p_j, r_j, d_j)$ for $j < n$ is feasible when there are start times $s_0, \dots, s_{n-1} \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $r_j \le s_j$ and $s_j + p_j \le d_j$ for every $j < n$, and for all $a < b < n$ either $s_a + p_a \le s_b$ or $s_b + p_b \le s_a$.

results.title: Single-machine scheduling with release times and deadlines as a decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: SINGLE-MACHINE SCHEDULING WITH RELEASE TIMES AND DEADLINES is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of release-deadlines instances, to a feasible instance. Bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.

results.title: SINGLE-MACHINE SCHEDULING WITH RELEASE TIMES AND DEADLINES is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The decision problem SINGLE-MACHINE SCHEDULING WITH RELEASE TIMES AND DEADLINES belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
